Name: Trolley - An Ecosystem Expansion
Author: cajcbell
Description:
[center][img]https://i.imgur.com/qx1UYTC.png[/img][/center]

[center][color=#D4D4D8][size=2][i]This is a re-release and overhaul of the [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/40376]Ecosystem Superpack Expansion[/url]. [/i][/size][/color][/center]
[center][/center]
[center][color=#D4D4D8][size=2][i]But wait, wasn't that expansion already a revamp of some existing mods?? Yes... apparently I love doing big project overhauls... the best way to think of it is this:  [/i][/size][/color][/center]
[center][list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][size=2][i]Originally, individual NPCs were released as separate mods. [/i][/size][/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][size=2][i]Then they were stitched together into ESE i.e. a "superpack"[/i][/size][/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][size=2][i]Trolley polishes it all together into an actual expansion[/i][/size][/color][/*]
[/list][/center]
[center][/center]
[center][color=#D4D4D8][size=2][i]Once again, characters and locations may seem familiar, but everything has been rewritten and will play out differently than before.[/i][/size][/color][/center]
[center][/center]
[center][color=#D4D4D8][size=2][i]Major bug fixes have also been implemented -  Please see below for installation instructions.[/i][/size][/color][/center]
[center][/center]
[center][color=#D4D4D8][size=2][i][b]No AI was used in the creation of ANY part of this mod. Thank you![/b][/i][/size][/color][/center]
[line]

[center][img]https://i.imgur.com/eb9JMc3.png[/img][/center]

[center][color=#D4D4D8][size=4]Explore down an old trolley line into new ecosystems. Meet new NPCs, shopkeepers, and a whole series of little features that expands the original flavor of the game![/size][/color][/center]

[center][list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][size=5][b]4 main areas[/b], with 10 maps total for immersion/interconnected spaces. [/size][/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][size=5][b]5 full NPCs [/b](including two romances, one roommate option).[/size][/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][size=5][b]3 shopkeepers[/b] which exchange rare and useful items[/size][/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][size=5]In total, [b]35 events[/b] to see, and [b]600+ lines of dialogue[/b][/size][/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][size=5]1 new crop, and [b]a handful of items, recipes, and rewards[/b][/size][/color][/*]
[/list][/center]

[size=4][b]Mid-Save: [/b][/size]
[size=4]1. Did this save have ESE, FIASA, Canyonlands, or Ranger Taro installed?[/size]
[size=4]            - [b]If not[/b], download the file and unzip to your Mods folder. That's it![/size]
[size=4]                      - [b]If yes[/b], see below:[/size]
[spoiler][size=4]Unfortunately, this revamp got so massive that this mod is no longer compatible with previous versions. I tried to put some warning messages on ESE's mod page, but still apologize for the inconvenience. If you have a save where you've played through a lot of ESE, I do not recommend installing this expansion mid-save. [/size]

[center][size=4][i][b]What will happen?[/b][/i][/size][/center]
[size=4]Items and animals will get errored, character hearts will get reset, pathing will get confused, and overall it will be a buggy, unhappy experience.[/size]

[size=4]THAT SAID, if you had ESE (or others) installed, but never really played through it (didn't see any cutscenes beyond opening, didn't marry anybody, didn't hatch any new animals, etc), then follow these instructions:[/size]

[size=4]1. [b]Completely delete all folders[/b] of ESE, Canyonlands, FIASA, and Ranger Taro from your Mods folder.[/size]
[size=4]2. [b]Load up the game, and let SMAPI run[/b] through a bunch of yellow text (this is SMAPI deleting the maps, characters, etc from your save). [/size]
[size=4]3. [b]Play the save at LEAST through one day[/b], so that your farmer goes to bed and saves the game again.[/size]
[size=4]4. [b]You can now install Trolley (somewhat) safely[/b]. Total lack of bugs is not guaranteed.[/size][/spoiler]

[left]Despite being a "medium-sized" expansion, impact on the vanilla game is minimal. Each of the entrances to the expansion are about 1-5 tiles wide, in hidden and under-utilized spots. It has been playtested with every major expansion, most custom NPCs, and any mod that changes the map of the desert/forest/beach. It was also modified in preparation for 1.7, with the goal of updating it immediately upon release.[/left]

[spoiler][size=4][b]What makes this version different than the previous ESE, and standalone mods?[/b][/size]
[size=4][b]-[/b][/size]
Most importantly, each iteration involves a massive improvement in coding, art, maps, and general mod-creation skills. I am an amateur coder who who learned how to make mods by practicing. Looking back at the first iteration of Ranger Taro for instance, means looking back at a laughable number of weird mistakes and bugs. There's a lot of charm in those older mods, and nothing particularly game-breaking about them, they just lack a certain level of quality. I had no freaking clue what I was doing, and found it miraculous that maps loaded at all, and that characters walked when they were supposed to walk.
-
For ESE in particular, it was my dream to pull together these individual NPCs into a bigger mod. But it was a way bigger task than I was prepared for, and I cut corners in some ways - and in other ways, was waaaay too clever about the solution. This led to weird coding that broke some multiplayer saves, and compatibility issues where I had no idea how to solve bugs. It was more of an experiment than anything else, and through making ESE I learned SO much more about how this all works.
[size=4][b]-[/b][/size]
[size=4][b]The list of improvements from ESE to Trolley is... big. So consider this a general overview:[/b][/size]

[list]
[*]Maps shifted around to make more geographical sense and fit together better[/*]
[*]Maps improved in every way[/*]
[*] Connecting maps added[/*]
[*]Character sprites and portraits improved[/*]
[*]Character dialogue and event writing improved[/*]
[*]Events completely restructured for each character[/*]
[*]New characters added[/*]
[*]Some items and animals removed (see below)[/*]
[*]Better mod compatibility testing and general community assets[/*]
[*]Some puzzles (in the canyons) simplified and streamlined[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b][i]Why were the farm animals removed?? [/i][/b][/size]
[b][i]-[/i][/b]
One major change with Trolley is the removal of farm animals. In Canyonlands and ESE,the player could hatch Desert Tortoises and Island Turtles in the barn and coop. To be honest, they were not well-implemented in the first place, and the resulting goods - pickled eggs, for example - were redundant with other widely used mods like Cornucopia. Rather than spending a lot of time improving the animals, I decided to focus this mod elsewhere - exploration and stories. In the future, I am interested in bringing the turtles back as a standalone mod, and think the tortoise makes the most sense as a pet. 

[i][b][size=4]Why were character changes made??[/size][/b][/i]
-

I don't know, gosh! Just kidding, but this is something I am making fun of myself for. I LOVE character writing, editing, and curating. For some NPCs (like Ranger Taro), this means every iteration has her story dialed in a little more, with the "twist" either a little more/less obvious. For other NPCs (like Koda), she may feel like an entirely different character, with a lot of events cut off. In my opinion, this is because her events were way too grandiose and "extra" before. I mean, the player was off on a solo adventure exploring an unnamed island at 6-hearts before. You know what Leah's 6-heart is? She shows up at the farm and gifts you her sculpture. It's less than a minute long, and imo has twice the meaning. So now that adventure is reserved for Koda's 10-heart, and she has much more interaction with her family and other villagers. All changes followed this logic of further matching, and adding to, the vanilla game.[/spoiler]

[center][color=#D4D4D8][size=4][b]The best way to get started is to stumble upon the maps naturally... but they are far away from the Farm! See below for hints on each entrance.[/b][/size][/color][/center]
[center][color=#D4D4D8][size=4][b]-[/b][/size][/color][/center]
[center][color=#D4D4D8][size=4][b]Forest:[/b][/size][/color][/center]
[center][spoiler][color=#D4D4D8]The forest entrance is at the bottom left corner of Cindersap Forest, right above the bridge to the Flower Dance. If you use Ornithologist Guild, head to the building and you'll see the entrance[/color][/spoiler]

[size=4][b]Beach:[/b][/size]
[spoiler][color=#D4D4D8]The beach entrance is next to the pile of driftwood on the northwest side of the beach, heading into the bushes. [/color][/spoiler]

[b][size=4]Desert:[/size][/b]
[spoiler][color=#D4D4D8]The desert entrance is found by walking left off the map along the sidewalk. There are no longer requirements for the entrance to appear, although of course you will have to take the bus to the desert first. There is a second way to the canyons by heading north from the Trolley station, but be warned - it's dangerous! This does mean that Trolley adds a way to walk  to the desert early, if you're brave enough.

Note: There's a special bush hidden in the canyon maze that will give you one "rainpuff" a day. Put it into a seedmaker and see what comes out![/color][/spoiler]
